Cangji (V05)

Region (English scoring-table grouping): Haless.

In one sentence: Begin with Harimari monasteries on a high plateau, kindle spiritfire to restore the wastes, free bound mages, and decide what kind of power Cangji will become in Haless.

Story: High | Mission-tree length: Long (46 direct V05 missions) | Mission-tree update: the local Mod supports EU4 v1.37.5.0; an official 2026 diary discusses the redesign | Uniqueness: Very high | Tedium: Medium-high (few exits from the plateau and late cross-region objectives) | Early pressure: Medium | Expansion: High from the midgame onward

Those the Plateau Left Behind

In 1444 Cangji is a Harimari-led highland monarchy, adherent to High Philosophy and accepting Plateau Rünsukhi culture, with its capital on the plateau. The history file records Monarch Xuanjue, heir Huiju, and old friendships and rivalries with nearby powers. The country already has a reserve of spells at the start, but has not yet spread spiritfire monasteries across the land. [Local history script]

An official development diary traces the monasteries' distant origin to Harimari explorers who left Jiantsiang roughly twelve centuries earlier and became stranded on the plateau. This helps explain why Ashwoven practitioners connect fire, water, spiritual cultivation, and survival. The Rünsukhi are not merely scenery: early missions recognize their knowledge while also exposing the power distance between Harimari monasteries and other residents of the plateau. The diary's origin account and mission narrative complement one another, but this recollection alone does not establish an exact founding date. [Official development diary] [Local narrative text]

The offline Wiki has no independently readable country-history page for Cangji. Related entries identify it as a Lotus Seat polity and mention the connection between the Rünsukhi and Ashwoven Harimari. These are identity clues, not enough to construct a complete pre-1444 chronology. This article therefore relies chiefly on current in-game narrative for plateau life and early tensions, and does not present later mission outcomes as established history. [Wiki] [Local narrative text]

Spiritfire Extends a Mountain Outward

Cangji's defining feature is its Spiritfire magic project. Spiritfire comes from the spirit world; monasteries and braziers use it for defense, cultivation, and warfare. Project progress strengthens the Eternal Cinder Monasteries, Khaaz-Monks, and War Mages. This is not ordinary province bonuses with a magical label: the player organizes the country around monastery placement, highland development, and specialized troops. Project unlocks and upgrades still require missions and investment; late-campaign capabilities are not free starting resources. [Local script] [Local narrative text]

Early missions call for igniting the Undying Flame at the ruins, investigating the spirit world beyond the plateau, and bringing Eagle Riders and Khaaz-Monks down from the mountains. Another line confronts the Command's anti-magic korashi shackles: Cangji studies how to disable them in order to free the mages they bind. This struggle has identifiable victims and cannot be reduced to a territorial dispute between two states. At the same time, missions demand that the country drive out spirits, deal with Facestealers, and control mountain passes; a defensive story soon becomes interwoven with regional conquest. [Local narrative text] [Local script]

In the middle phase, the country incorporates Rünsukhi culture, outside groups, and newly conquered lands into an empire. The player must navigate the tension between protection and coexistence on one hand and monastery-centered rule on the other; the text does not establish that every incorporated group thereby receives equal autonomy. Spiritfire's environmental engineering also carries risks: suppressing the local spirits too aggressively may cause a monastery fire, after which the country must calm them and rebuild cooperation. This disaster is a mission-driven future, not an event that has already happened in 1444. [Local narrative text]

The stages fit together clearly: early on, make the mountains, forts, and monasteries support one another while investing in mages and the project; once the country reaches the plains, military victory does not substitute for cultural and religious governance; when the spirit tide comes, knowledge first developed for the plateau must reach distant lands. Institutions built for one place acquire new purposes over time, making Cangji especially suited to players who enjoy watching a country's institutions change with its missions. [Local script] [Local narrative text]

The Name Changes; the Campaign Remains One

Events offer two renaming paths, Gozengun Raj and Cangzhou, and switch the subsequent non-generic missions. Both retain Tag V05; these are not two separate formable countries. The later campaign moves into Haless, contests Jianxusi and the coast, establishes markets and monasteries in the wastes, and ultimately attempts to repair the reality-rift caused by the spirit tide. Spiritfire thus changes from a local defense into a regional-governance and world-crisis response, with corresponding demands for territory, engineering, and magical expertise. [Local script] [Local narrative text]

Player reports praise the monasteries, multicultural integration, and summoned forces, while also mentioning expensive building prerequisites and late conquest objectives that can lengthen the campaign. These are experiences from particular versions; unit values and mission requirements must still be taken from the local scripts and the player's actual save. [Community opinion]

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 77/100 | Autocracy 69/100 | Magic–Artifice 95/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 96/100) | Pluralism 68/100. Phase shift: plateau monasteries (Expansion 42) → Haless and the wastes (Expansion 82).

The v2.1 value profile is Neutral (65/100), with a mixed trajectory. Freeing mages, restoring wasteland, and calming spirits disturbed by spiritfire are positive evidence; monastic hierarchy, the Facestealer-clearing objective, and engineering risks constrain the assessment. Conquest itself is not penalized. The country suits players who enjoy highland building, magical research, cross-cultural governance, and long-range expansion. It is a poor fit for players who only want a short conquest campaign or do not want to manage monastery projects and late cross-region objectives. [Local script] [Local narrative text]

See the evidence record for source locations, fixed Wiki revisions, and unresolved points.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect display units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here. Suspicious percentages and script-valued effects require separate review; raw values are shown below.

Cangji (V05) — Cangji Ideas

Set ID: V05_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

    trigger = {
        tag = V05 #Cangji

Cangji Traditions

  • Advisor cost: -10% (advisor_cost; raw value -0.1).

  • Ruler administrative skill: +1 (monarch_admin_power; raw value 1).

1. The Lone Lotus Seat

The tale of the Ashwoven Harimari is one of opportunity, betrayal, and intrigue. Scions of the Eastern Lotus Court of Lianzhou, a meager cadet branch of the Undying Flame dynasty known as the Ashen Soul embarked upon a research expedition in 277 AA to the mythical expanse of Gozengun, following tales of the wonders of northern spirit magic. To reach their destination in the southern Rünsukhi plateau, they would require the approval of the Kingdom of Guwaamud, an ancient rival of Lianzhou. Amidst a temporary peace between the two powers, the expedition managed to set out upon a journey of discovery.

The expedition was fruitful, and much was learned. The Ashen Expedition began preparations for their triumphant return. However, in the summer of 282 AA, a brutal war had begun between Lianzhou and Guwaamud. No longer assured safe passage and isolated from any semblance of a supply line, the decision was made. Upon the plateau would be founded Cangyuan, the Lotus Seat of the Harimraj, and its loneliest outpost.

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).

2. Evoke the Ashen Soul

The Ashen Soul dynasty from which the Ashwoven Harimari gained their name is a peculiar one, with coats as white as ash and innate magical power resting within their illustrious fur. With a fervent curiosity and unquenchable thirst for knowledge, the Ashen Soul seamlessly filled the role of scholar-gentry, organizing several expeditions upon the Gowon Sea and eventually venturing north of the Demon Hills into the unknown.

One aspect of this endless pursuit of knowledge was an unrivaled aptitude for the arcane among the Eastern Harimraj. Boasting mastery of fire and water, the Ashen Soul evoke sorcerous blood to mold the immaterial into material, to gather the vital chi of the elements and wield the result with ferocity and grace befitting the twofold tigers of Rahen.

  • Leader land shock: +1 (leader_land_shock; raw value 1).

  • English translation: [Country.GetMageName]: +5% (mages_loyalty_modifier; raw value 0.05).

3. Tian Zhu

The glistening sands have long since been blessed with ample geodes of a special variety of gemstone known by locals as Divine Agate, formerly mined as a novelty for jewelry or other meager decor. However, with the advent of chi-based research among the Rünsukhi, it became clear that Divine Agate held special properties concerning the storage and release of chi. A sufficiently empowered agate, when worn, possesses remarkable protective powers, warding adverse spirits and helping oneself achieve balance, within and without.

These charms became known as Tian Zhu, or “Heaven’s Beads,” and have become a popular source of tangible–though very temporary–protection amidst the treacherous wastes of Gozengun.

  • True faith tolerance: +1 (tolerance_own; raw value 1).

  • Trade steering: +10% (trade_steering; raw value 0.1).

4. Khaaz-Monks of the Blazing Claw

Despite their loathsome persistence, little is known about the spirits of Haless, entities that have razed villages on a whim, caused castles to fall in mere days, and ravaged the minds of the brightest minds to ever live. The endless pursuit to understand and ultimately banish spirits led to many harimari of the way of the Blazing Claw, historical residents of Lianzhou, to seek passage north to the fabled lands of Gozengun. It was said that there upon a high plateau, monks could recite words of power known as mantras to abjure and ward their secluded monasteries against the many spirits they face each day.

Many of the Blazing Claw chose to take advantage of the ill-fated Ashen Expedition in 277 AA, offering their services as guards or schleppers in hopes of learning these legendary techniques. Upon the expedition’s arrival in the year 279 AA, the monks of the Blazing Claw began to fervently study the art of Khaaz, ultimately mastering the technique over the centuries and wielding it with a tigerlike ferocity, evoking pink and blue psychic flames alongside traditional Xiaken martial arts to banish ethereal and mortal alike. They earned the title of Khaaz-Monks, acting as warrior-exorcists in times of spiritual strife.

  • Infantry combat ability: +10% (infantry_power; raw value 0.1).

5. Monastic Schism

Though reverence of the High Gods is, by all rights, the official religious doctrine of Cangji, worship and dedication in accordance with the tenets of High Philosophy is typically localized to secluded monasteries and harimari mage-pagodas. Due to the relative minority status harimari hold within the Lotus Seat, the vast majority of the domain adheres to traditional Rünsukhi values, though as the years passed, more and more Rünsukhi locals began to set their sights upon Kartya.

This monastic division has led to a separation of roles between harimari and Rünsukhi believers–the Ashwoven Harimari spend much of the year in quiet contemplation of Dekhana, or "ascertaining," whilst the Rünsukhi at large, who often lack proper education of specific philosophical doctrine, take a more active role in the faith through the art of Pichka, or "pursuing."

  • global_manpower_modifier: +15% (global_manpower_modifier; raw value 0.15).

6. Graveyard of Cogs

Many archaeological sites of clockwork treasures and marvels litter the surface of the Southern Rünsukhi Plateau, full of trinkets and tidbits the likes of which we can barely comprehend. These trinkets and relics are the subject of much study by the Ashwoven gentry-scholars, and over centuries of study and refinement, clockwork architecture began to make an appearance among mage-pagodas, powering and facilitating the operation of many arcane contraptions. Though this technology remains incomprehensible to the public, mages of the Ashen Soul have made countless breakthroughs regarding the discernment of ancient, otherworldly technology.

  • Technology cost: -5% (technology_cost; raw value -0.05).

7. Low Temple of the North

The various peoples of Haless were each forced to adapt to survive and overcome the whims of spirits. The Yanglam tribes of the Lupulan pursued appeasement and coexistence with their mythical Great Spirit, whilst the peoples of Rahen and Yanshen chose to gather around the masterworks of the High Gods to bask in the divine mercy offered to all that follow in the High Gods’ footsteps.

Now, we walk upon soil and sands that the High Gods did not tread. This does not mean, however, that we must fend for ourselves. The Ashen Expedition possessed the foresight to bring along a single ember of the Undying Flame, preserving its warding powers for the journey ahead, and nurturing it upon a brazier located in the inner sanctum of the Low Temple of Cangyuan. This ember would spark a grand blaze and project a powerful magical ward, preventing spirits from moving within its radius unhindered.

  • National unrest: -2 (global_unrest; raw value -2).
